invariants.avoid: Nested reactive objects remain proxies. Keep the blanket matcher off until value types can be resolved.
invariants.fixHint: Keep the reactive object whole, or convert it with toRefs before destructuring so each key stays a ref.

source.paraphrase: Destructuring a reactive primitive property loses reactivity. Extracted nested objects remain reactive proxies.

invariants.why: Destructured primitives lose reactivity, but nested object proxies retain it. This matcher cannot determine the extracted value type.

invariants.avoid: Pinia actions can be extracted directly. Keep the blanket matcher off until state and actions can be resolved.
invariants.fixHint: Wrap the store in storeToRefs first, then destructure. Actions can come off the store directly.

source.paraphrase: Use storeToRefs for reactive state and getters. Bound store actions can be destructured directly.

invariants.why: Destructured state loses reactivity, but bound actions may be destructured directly. This matcher cannot distinguish actions from state.

invariants.avoid: A comment or a cast beside the call does not add a type. Only an explicit type argument counts.
invariants.fixHint: Write the type argument: ref<string | null>(null). The checker then accepts later assignments of that type.

source.paraphrase: ref infers from its argument. null and undefined infer to a type that rejects every later value.

invariants.why: An untyped ref(null) narrows to a type that holds nothing, so the first real assignment fails the build far from the cause.

invariants.avoid: Passing a callback is supported and is not matched. The zero-argument matcher cannot establish whether later code needs the DOM update.
invariants.fixHint: If later code needs the updated DOM, await or return the promise, or pass that work as a callback.

source.paraphrase: Wait for DOM updates by passing a callback to nextTick or by awaiting its promise.

invariants.why: A floating nextTick lets the next lines run against the old DOM, so measurements and focus land on stale nodes.

invariants.avoid: More segments do not help. Any plus inside push arguments is string-built routing, even with a shared base prefix. The receiver must end in router, for example router, this.$router or useRouter(). A push on an array is not matched. A router held under another name is not matched.
invariants.fixHint: Push a named route with a params object: push({ name: "user", params: { id } }). Renames then fail the build instead of the router.

source.paraphrase: Named routes with params keep navigation checkable. Concatenated paths hide renames until a user clicks.

invariants.why: A renamed path breaks every concatenated push silently, and the failure only shows when a user reaches that screen.

invariants.avoid: Moving the async getter into the options form (get: async () => ... or async get()) still returns a Promise. A sync setter beside it does not help.
invariants.fixHint: Load the data in a watcher (or watchEffect) that writes a ref, then compute from that ref. VueUse computedAsync is the packaged form of the same idea.

source.locator: Computed Properties, Getters should be side-effect free
source.paraphrase: Computed getters only compute and return a value. Do not make async requests in them; use watchers for side effects.

invariants.why: An async getter returns a Promise, so every reader and the template see a Promise instead of the value, and each dependency change fires another request.
